newsitem.title: USA: Moody's may review Argentina ratings in 12-18 mos.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may review Argentina ratings in 12-18 mos.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service may place Argentina's B1 sovereign rating on review for possible upgrade sometime in the next 12 to 18 months, but it is not currently considering a ratings change, a Moody's analyst said.
In a press release on Wednesday, the agency had said its outlook for Argentina's rating is "improving."

"What this explicitly means ... is that there is at least a 50-50 chance that within 12 to 18 months there will be a review for a possible upgrade," said Kristin Lindow, a Moody's senior analyst who covers Argentina.

Argentine newspaper El Cronista on Thursday said Moody's had raised its outlook on Argentina to "positive" from "stable." But Lindow said Moody's prefers to avoid such terms in describing a sovereign ratings outlook.
"You have to read from the tone. The tone of our opinion used to be stable," she said. "This says 'improving' ... which is positive."
In Wednesday's release, Moody's said world liquity and improved investor sentiment had lifted prospects for successful refinancings in Argentina.
In addition, Argentina's reinforced tax administration should help diminish the need for additional foreign-currency, public sector debt, Moody's said.
"However, private sector foreign debt is likely to expand rapidly as investment will outpace national savings," it said.
Moody's said it was not currently reviewing Argentina for a possible ratings change.
Argentina carries a BB foreign currency rating from Standard & Poor's.
